faq.q: How do I make a product post that gets a second look?
faq.a: Start with your product photo, or with a frame that already has a border. Add your words after download. When that square works, make the next one from the same photo.

faq.q: What should a product post include so people stop?
faq.a: Lead with a sharp photo of the product and a hook in the first line. Try a wider scene as the next post. A real item beats a vague graphic.

faq.q: How often should a small shop post product photos?
faq.a: Pick a pace you can keep when orders pile up, such as three finished photos a week. One product photo can supply those squares, and you still reply to the comments.

faq.q: How much does a social ad image cost?
faq.a: Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. Each image is 24 credits, shown before it runs. A failed image returns those credits.

faq.q: Where can I use the square file?
faq.a: The download is square, so it fits a lot of feed posts. In each ad tool, check that your words are not cut off. It does not turn itself into a tall story or a wide banner.

faq.q: Can I put my headline on the image?
faq.a: Yes. Add a short headline on the image, or type that line in your ad editor when you want the price set there.

faq.q: Can I make several scenes from one photo?
faq.a: Yes. Build different settings from the same product photo and compare them before you spend on the ad.

faq.q: Do I have to label the image as AI?
faq.a: Follow the label your ad account asks for, then post the square. Rules differ by app and by country. For a looser phone-shot look, see [casual phone-style product photos](page:tpl-ugc).
